name: Navigation App
description: An entry on the navigation rail: a named group of sidebars, or the stand-in for an installed app (or Other) whose place, title, mark, sidebars and visibility it changes. The rail lists these first; every sidebar none of them claims is still reachable, grouped under the installed app it belongs to.

fields.label: Title
fields.description: What the rail's tooltip and the sidebar header call this app. Filled in from the installed app when one is picked.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: A disabled record changes nothing: it claims none of its modules, and an installed app it stands for is drawn as if it had no record. To take an app off the rail, use Hide from Rail.

fields.label: Rail Position
fields.description: Where this app sits when it is not in its default place: "top", or the key of the app it follows (app:erpnext, navigation-app:Finance). Left blank, an installed app's record sits where the app would (install order, Other last), and an app of the site's own at the top. Manage Rail sets this; it writes a position only for the apps that move.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Drawn on the rail when there is no logo. Left blank with no logo either, an installed app keeps the logo its code gives it.

fields.label: Logo
fields.description: Drawn on the rail in place of the icon.

fields.label: Modules
fields.description: The modules this app offers, in the order the rail's menus list them: drag rows to reorder. For an installed app in Add mode, these come first and the app's other modules follow in its default order: the order its shipped Dock gives them, leaving out the ones the Dock hides; else Home, or the one named after the app, first, then alphabetical. Listing a module the Dock hides puts it back. A module can belong to only one enabled app. A Category row is a heading over the modules after it, and a Spacer row a gap; a Category left last heads the app's other modules.

fields.label: Frontend URL
fields.description: An app with a frontend of its own, outside the desk, such as /helpdesk or /commons. Offered beside the app's modules and opened in the same tab. An app with a frontend and no modules opens it straight from the rail. Left blank, an installed app keeps the frontend its code declares.

fields.label: Frontend Label
fields.description: What the module list and the top menu call the frontend. Left blank, the app's title followed by "app".

fields.label: Roles
fields.description: Only people with one of these roles see the app on the rail. Left empty, everyone does. Either way, a module a person cannot open is not offered to them.

fields.label: Installed App
fields.description: Leave blank for a grouping of your own. Pick an installed app, or Other, to change that app's entry instead: this record takes its place on the rail. Only one enabled record can stand for each.

fields.label: Hide from Rail
fields.description: Takes the app off the rail for everyone. Its modules go with it rather than back to an installed app; they can still be opened by address.

fields.label: Modules Mode
fields.description: Add: the app keeps the modules it already has, after any listed below. Replace: only the modules listed below, in their order; the rest go to Other, except the ones its Dock hides, which stay off the rail.

fields.label: Apps Screen
fields.options:
One Icon
Icon per Module
Hidden
fields.description: How the Apps screen (/desk) shows this app, when Commons Settings arranges it from the Navigation Apps. One Icon: a single tile, opening the app. Icon per Module: a tile for each of its modules (and its frontend), in the order of its modules. Hidden: not on the Apps screen; it stays on the rail. Apps without a record show as one icon. An app taken off the rail is off the Apps screen too.
